item.title: Russia launches 339 drones at Ukraine after Kremlin rejects Easter ceasefire
item.description:
Russia launched 339 attack drones at Ukraine overnight into Wednesday, striking the western city of Lutsk and multiple other regions, just hours after the Kremlin dismissed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's proposal for a ceasefire during Orthodox Easter. Zelenskyy called the barrage Moscow's "response to diplomacy."

Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 298 of the drones, but at least 20 struck targets across 11 locations, according to Ukraine's Air Force. In Lutsk, drones hit an industrial facility and a warehouse operated by Nova Poshta, Ukraine's leading courier service, and damaged a residential building. No casualties were reported there. Fires also broke out in the western city of Khmelnytskyi after drones struck a commercial enterprise.

item.title: Macron and Takaichi align on Hormuz crisis, rare earths in Tokyo summit
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held their first full bilateral summit in Tokyo on Wednesday, with the Middle East conflict and its fallout on global energy markets dominating an agenda that had originally been designed to deepen cooperation on nuclear energy and space innovation.

The meeting came on the second day of Macron's three-day visit to Japan — the first by a French president in more than a decade — and hours after the French leader took a pointed swipe at the Trump administration in front of Japanese business leaders.

item.title: UAE prepares to join coalition to reopen Strait of Hormuz by force
item.description: A growing coalition of nations led by Britain and France is racing to organize a multinational mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the critical shipping lane that Iran has effectively shut down since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran in late February. The effort has now drawn more than 30 countries into military planning talks, even as deep divisions over the broader war strategy were laid bare at a G7 foreign ministers meeting in France last week.

item.title: Shell in advanced talks to develop major gas fields in Venezuela
item.description:
Shell is in advanced negotiations with Venezuela's government to develop four large offshore natural gas areas near Trinidad and Tobago, in what would represent a major expansion of the energy giant's footprint in the country, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

The talks center on two of South America's largest offshore gas deposits, with combined reserves of roughly 20 trillion cubic feet. Shell is seeking access to three fields that form part of the 12-tcf Mariscal Sucre project off Venezuela's east coast — including the flagship 4.2-tcf Dragon field — as well as the 7.3-tcf Loran offshore field, which straddles the maritime border with Trinidad, according to two people familiar with the discussions.

item.title: Trump ties ceasefire talks to reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran has made international recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz a central condition for any ceasefire in the ongoing war with the United States and Israel, deepening a crisis that has upended global energy markets and sent oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel.

item.title: Trump to address nation on Iran as war enters day 33
item.description:
The U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its 33rd day on Wednesday, with Israel reporting it has carried out more than 800 combat sorties using approximately 16,000 munitions since Operation Roaring Lion began on February 28, while Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the 89th wave of its "True Promise-4" retaliatory campaign, deploying over 100 heavy missiles, combat drones, and around 200 rocket projectiles at U.S. and Israeli positions across the region.

President Donald Trump is set to deliver a national address at 9 p.m. ET Wednesday to provide what the White House called "an important update" on Iran, after saying Tuesday that U.S. forces would be "leaving soon" and predicting the conflict could end within two to three weeks.

item.title: Israel kills Hezbollah's Southern Front commander in Beirut naval strike
item.description: Israeli naval forces killed Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem, the commander of Hezbollah's Southern Front, in a strike on Beirut early Wednesday, the Israel Defense Forces announced. The attack on the Jnah district of the Lebanese capital was one of two Israeli strikes in the Beirut area overnight that killed at least seven people and wounded more than two dozen others, according to Lebanon's health ministry.

item.title: Macron reaffirms France won't join US-Israel war on Iran
item.description:
Speaking at a joint press conference with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo on Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron firmly restated that France has no role in the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran and was never asked to participate.

"It is absolutely true that France, which was not consulted and is not part of the military offensive launched by the United States and Israel, is not taking part," Macron told reporters, according to French news channel BFMTV.

item.title: Seizing Iran's uranium by force would risk casualties, experts warn
item.description:
Should the United States attempt to seize Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium by military force, the operation would require as many as 1,000 specially trained troops, carry radiation and chemical hazards, and likely result in casualties, according to experts and former government officials.

The warning, detailed in an Associated Press report from Vienna, underscores the tension between President Donald Trump's stated goal that Iran will "never have a nuclear weapon" and the practical difficulties of achieving it on the ground.

item.title: Trump demands Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz, threatens to 'obliterate' infrastructure
item.description: As the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its second month, Tehran has moved to formalize its control over the Strait of Hormuz, demanding international recognition of its sovereignty over the critical waterway as a condition for ending the conflict — a stance that has drawn sharp rebukes from Washington and rattled global energy markets.

item.title: UK to host 35-nation summit on reopening Strait of Hormuz
item.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Wednesday that the UK will host a virtual summit of approximately 35 countries on Thursday to discuss diplomatic and military steps to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway effectively shut down by the ongoing conflict between the US and Israel against Iran.

item.title: Macron warns U.S. exit from Iran without deal would be 'worst-case scenario'
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron used a visit to Tokyo on Wednesday to deliver a pointed critique of the Trump administration's handling of the Iran conflict, warning that a hasty American withdrawal from the Middle East without a diplomatic framework in place would amount to a worst-case scenario.

item.title: Italy recovers 19 bodies from migrant boat near Lampedusa
item.description: Italy's coast guard recovered the bodies of 19 migrants and rescued 58 survivors from a dinghy that broke down while attempting to cross the central Mediterranean from Libya, officials said on Wednesday. The vessel was intercepted on Tuesday night roughly 80 nautical miles south of the island of Lampedusa amid rough weather conditions.

item.title: Iran's Pezeshkian tells Americans his country 'harbors no enmity' toward them
item.description:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday released an open letter addressed to the American people, declaring that Iran "harbors no enmity" toward ordinary Americans and arguing that portraying Iran as a threat was "neither consistent with historical reality nor with present-day observable facts," according to Reuters and Iran's state-run Press TV.

The letter represents a direct diplomatic appeal to the U.S. public amid an ongoing military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran that began on February 28 and is now in its fifth week.

item.title: Iran now charging yuan and crypto tolls in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has transformed the world's most critical oil chokepoint into what shipping experts are calling a "de facto toll booth," formalizing a system in which vessels must pay fees and submit to vetting for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The development, confirmed by Bloomberg on Wednesday, shows the toll regime now extends to payments in Chinese yuan or stablecoins, with oil tankers facing a starting price of roughly $1 per barrel.

The IRGC-controlled process requires ships to contact intermediaries linked to the paramilitary force. Vessels must submit manifests, crew details, and destination information for what Lloyd's List Intelligence describes as "sanctions screening, cargo alignment checks" and "geopolitical vetting". Approved vessels receive a permit code and are escorted by an IRGC vessel along a northern route around Larak Island, closer to Iran's coastline, rather than the conventional central shipping lanes. Informal tolls of up to $2 million per voyage have been reported.

item.title: Artemis II lifts off, sending first crew to the Moon in over 50 years
item.description: NASA's Artemis II mission lifted off from Kennedy Space Center at 6:24 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, sending four astronauts on humanity's first crewed voyage to the Moon in more than half a century. Among the crew is Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, who became the first Canadian — and the first non-American — ever to fly on a lunar mission.

item.title: Russia vows continued aid to Cuba after first oil shipment in three months
item.description: The Trump administration permitted a sanctioned Russian-flagged oil tanker to dock in Cuba this week, breaking an effective fuel blockade that had plunged the island nation into its worst energy crisis in decades. The Anatoly Kolodkin arrived at the port of Matanzas on Monday carrying approximately 730,000 barrels of crude oil — roughly 100,000 metric tons — after a three-week voyage from Russia's Primorsk port.

item.title: Nepal charges 32 in $20M Everest helicopter rescue scam
item.description: Nepalese authorities have filed organized crime and fraud charges against 32 people in connection with a sprawling scheme that allegedly bilked international travel insurers out of nearly $20 million through fake helicopter rescues on Mount Everest and other Himalayan peaks.

item.title: Trump declares Iran war 'winding down' in primetime address
item.description:
President Trump delivered a primetime national address on Wednesday evening, telling Americans that the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran is "winding down" and that all military objectives have been met — 33 days after Operation Epic Fury began on February 28.

The speech, broadcast from the White House at 9 p.m. ET, capped a day in which Trump escalated his rhetoric on multiple fronts, claiming on Truth Social that Iran's president had requested a ceasefire, threatening NATO allies over the Strait of Hormuz, and telling Reuters in an interview that the U.S. would be "out of Iran pretty quickly" but could return for "spot hits" if necessary.

item.title: Trump declares Iran war 'nearing completion' in primetime address
item.description: President Donald Trump used a rare primetime address Wednesday night to tell Americans the month-old war in Iran is "nearing completion," projecting another two to three weeks of military involvement while simultaneously threatening devastating escalation if Tehran does not meet his demands.
